scope: Supplement to the client TLS remediation record: existing Tunnel infrastructure, private-feedback maintenance transport, and two older preview asset distributions.

server_upgrade.execution: A separate user-authorized maintenance conversation performed the server upgrades. The coordinating Airtap conversation independently inspected the resulting official running processes.
server_upgrade.verification_scope: Read-only snapshots of the actual process executable versions and their service units; checking an installed package or a temporary test binary alone was not counted as an upgraded official instance.
server_upgrade.airtap_runtime_boundary: The default Airtap phone-control relay runs on Cloudflare Workers and Durable Objects, without a cloudflared dependency. Upgrading these other Tunnel services does not itself update Airtap Android, CLI or third-party TLS runtimes.

feedback_maintenance_transport.policy: Load the shipped CLI transport from the fixed source-distribution layout. Preserve system CA and hostname validation, then reject known compromised public keys across the verified chain before target HTTP headers or body.
feedback_maintenance_transport.proxy_boundary: Proxy credentials are confined to HTTP CONNECT; the target maintenance Bearer and report body are not sent before target TLS validation. No automatic direct fallback after proxy failure.
feedback_maintenance_transport.failure_behavior: Missing transport or unavailable chain verification fails closed. Redirects are not followed. Definite certificate rejection before HTTP is not_dispatched; certificate failure after an HTTP attempt remains unknown. No automatic retry of maintenance mutations and no legacy urllib fallback.
feedback_maintenance_transport.installation_requirement: Use the complete updated source distribution, preserving relay/service/reports.py and cli/airtap.py at their relative locations. Copying reports.py alone is insufficient.

earlier_failure.description: The initial environment invoked the default javac and its contract-test compilation exited with an error. The same service suite passed after selecting the configured JDK. The failed run is retained.

checks.scope: Local ephemeral TLS/CONNECT endpoints and source checks; these do not claim a real private-report CRUD workflow, a new source ZIP export, or a complete product regression.

public_negative_auth_probe.scope: Read-only request to a nonexistent report through the fixed transport; no valid maintenance credential or mutation.

older_preview_updates.deployment_status_note: Resumed the exact reviewed frozen state; final deployment succeeded and pending pointer is clear. Public CLI and guide bytes match reviewed SHA256, and discovery retained the original service identity.

prepared_integrity.configuration_changes: Only the new frozen-directory references and three artifact version/hash variables differ.

checks.wait_ready_result: Each deterministic TLS failure terminates after one status attempt, without sleep or retry.

limits: Publishing a fixed CLI or guide does not replace files already downloaded by personal agents. Those clients require an actual update and verification.
These compatibility asset updates do not upgrade older installed Android APKs. Existing device identities and pairings must be preserved during a supported client upgrade or migration.

Older invitations do not gain code38 phone-bound expected artifact hashes. The device preview still needs independently trusted expected hashes before following downloaded guidance or executing the CLI.
Direct HTTPS tools, MCP clients, browser runtimes and other applications require their own certificate-policy review; CLI protection does not automatically transfer to them.
Known-key denial is a targeted mitigation, not a claim that every certificate, device or runtime is safe, nor evidence that an attack occurred or did not occur.
Server service readiness and local regression tests do not establish all application workflows, new-user setup, or long-term connection reliability.
The legacy service public checks encountered transient timeouts before succeeding; this one-network-vantage result is not a claim of universal or uninterrupted reachability.

privacy.included: Public code and artifact hashes, aggregate test counts, release versions and bounded verification outcomes.
excluded: Internal domains, IP addresses, hostnames and service identifiers
Private filesystem paths and deployment state
Credentials, certificate private keys and pairing data
Raw logs, screenshots, report contents and user data
